title: Finite-stalk specialization criterion for local constancy
statement: Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme (quasi-compact and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]) [def-pc-scheme], $\Lambda$ a finite commutative ring, and $G$ a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Suppose every geometric stalk $G_{\bar s}$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] is finite as a set, and for every geometric point $\bar s$ and every geometric point $\bar t$ of $S_{(\bar s)}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], the specialization map $G_{\bar s}\to G_{\bar t}$ is bijective. Here specialization is induced by restriction of pointed etale neighbourhood germs through $S_{(\bar s)}\to S$. Then $G$ is finite locally constant: there is an etale covering $\{U_i\to S\}$ and finite $\Lambda$-modules $M_i$ with $G|_{U_i}\cong\underline{M_i}$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] [def-constructible-locally-constant].

source.place: Tag 0GKC, label lemma-characterize-locally-constant-module, (2) implies (1), finite coefficient ring and Noetherian base

proof.text: Fix a geometric point $\bar s$ and put $M=G_{\bar s}$, a finite $\Lambda$-module. Use the small representative category of affine pointed neighbourhoods specified in the strict-henselization construction; affine shrinking and cofilteredness make its opposite filtered. The elementwise filtered-colimit description of the stalk represents every $m\in M$ by a section $\sigma_m$ on a common pointed neighbourhood. The finitely many relations $\sigma_0=0$, $\sigma_{m+n}=\sigma_m+\sigma_n$ and $\sigma_{am}=a\sigma_m$, for $m,n\in M$ and $a\in\Lambda$, hold in the stalk. The equality criterion in the filtered colimit and common refinement make all these relations hold on one neighbourhood $(U,\bar u)$. Thus $m\mapsto\sigma_m$ is a module map $M\to G(U)$ inducing identity on the chosen stalk. The constant-sheaf adjunction gives a morphism $\varphi:\underline M\to G|_U$. Shrink $U$ to an affine pointed neighbourhood. Via the inverse-image stalk comparison and the constant-stalk identification, $\varphi_{\bar u}$ is bijective.

source.place: Tag 0GKC, lemma-characterize-locally-constant-module, proof of (2) implies (1); finite presentation paragraph, expanded by the finite module operation table

proof.text: We record the pullback calculation used below (Stacks 0GJ6, lemma-specialization-map-pullback). Let $g:T\to S$ be a morphism, $\bar x$ a geometric point of $T$, and $\bar z$ a geometric point of $T_{(\bar x)}$; write $p_T:T_{(\bar x)}\to T$ and $\bar y=p_T\circ\bar z$. For each affine pointed etale neighbourhood $(W,\bar w)$ of $g\bar x$, the base change $(W\times_S T,(\bar w,\bar x))$ is a pointed neighbourhood of $\bar x$. Choose an affine pointed refinement; its limit projection followed by the refinement map defines $T_{(\bar x)}\to W\times_S T$. Two choices agree after a common affine refinement, by cofilteredness and compatibility of the limit projections. These maps commute with every pointed neighbourhood map, so their composites to $W$ form a cone. The defining limit gives $h:T_{(\bar x)}\to S_{(g\bar x)}$ with these projections. Put $\bar t=h\bar z$. For a section $a\in F(W)$ of an abelian sheaf $F$ on $S$, pullback gives the unit section on $W\times_S T$. Specializing its germ at $\bar x$ gives its germ at the point induced by $\bar z$. The inverse-image germ comparison sends this to the germ of $a$ at the point of $W$ induced by $h\bar z$, which is exactly $sp_F(a_{g\bar x})$. Every source stalk element has such a representative, by the same comparison. Thus $c_{g,\bar y,F}\circ sp_{g^{-1}F}=sp_F\circ c_{g,\bar x,F}$. The abelian calculation applies to the underlying abelian sheaf of a module sheaf.

source.place: Tag 0GJ6, label lemma-specialization-map-pullback, omitted proof expanded using limit projections and germs

proof.text: Naturality and constants are direct germ calculations (Stacks 0GJ2, section-specialization). For a sheaf morphism $\alpha:F\to H$ and a section $a\in F(W)$, specializing $\alpha_W(a)$ and applying $\alpha$ to the specialized germ of $a$ both give $(\alpha_W(a))_{\bar t}$. Hence $sp_H\circ\alpha_{\bar s}=\alpha_{\bar t}\circ sp_F$. For the constant sheaf $\underline M$, represent $m$ by the canonical constant section labelled $m$ on the final neighbourhood. Specialization leaves this section unchanged; under the constant-stalk identification it therefore sends $m$ to $m$.

source.place: Tag 0GJ2, label section-specialization, germ definition and functoriality

proof.text: Let $E$ be the set of points $x\in U$ at which $\varphi$ is bijective on a geometric stalk. The natural comparison between stalk functors at geometric points with the same image, identity on constant stalks, makes this condition independent of the chosen geometric point. For any $y\leadsto x$ in $U$, lift a geometric point over $y$ to $U_{(\bar x)}$ using the geometric-specialization lifting lemma. The pullback calculation of step 2 identifies specialization for $G|_U$ with one of the bijective specialization maps assumed for $G$; step 3 gives $sp_{G|_U}\circ\varphi_{\bar x}=\varphi_{\bar y}\circ sp_{\underline M}$. The latter specialization is identity on $M$ by step 3. Write $b=sp_{G|_U}$, which is bijective by step 2 and the hypothesis; the displayed equation then gives $\varphi_{\bar y}=b\circ\varphi_{\bar x}$ under the constant-stalk identifications. Consequently $\varphi_{\bar x}$ is bijective if and only if $\varphi_{\bar y}$ is bijective. Thus $E$ is stable under both specializations and generalizations and contains $u$.

source.place: Tag 0GKC, lemma-characterize-locally-constant-module, proof of (2) implies (1); bijectivity locus paragraph

proof.text: The affine scheme $U$ is Noetherian: its map to $S$ is etale, hence locally of finite presentation and therefore locally of finite type (a finite presentation has finitely many algebra generators); the locally-Noetherian finite-type lemma applies, and the affine-scheme quasi-compactness lemma [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs] gives quasi-compactness. Its irreducible components $C_1,\ldots,C_r$ are finite in number. Remove their finite closed union for those $C_i$ not containing $u$, obtaining an open neighbourhood $V$ of $u$. Each remaining $C_i$ has a generic point $\eta_i$ by sobriety of schemes. Since $u\in C_i$, generalization stability gives $\eta_i\in E$; specialization stability then gives every point of $C_i$ in $E$. The components cover $U$, so $V\subseteq E$.

source.place: Tag 0GKC, lemma-characterize-locally-constant-module, proof of (2) implies (1); component shrinking paragraph

proof.text: On $V$, every geometric stalk of $\varphi$ is bijective. Apply the stalkwise-isomorphism criterion to the underlying set sheaves to obtain an isomorphism on each section object. Its inverse is $\Lambda$-linear: for $b,b^{\prime}$ in the target, apply injectivity of $\varphi$ to the identities $\varphi(a+a^{\prime})=b+b^{\prime}$ and $\varphi(\lambda a)=\lambda b$. The componentwise inverses commute with restriction: from $r_G\circ\varphi_W=\varphi_{W^{\prime}}\circ r_M$, compose with the two inverses to get $\varphi_{W^{\prime}}^{-1}\circ r_G=r_M\circ\varphi_W^{-1}$. Hence $G|_V\simeq\underline M$ as module sheaves. Repeat for every point of $S$, choosing a geometric point above it; the resulting etale neighbourhoods cover $S$ and each $M$ is finite. If $S$ is empty, the empty covering already gives the conclusion.
